ponder.cbbees.mechanical_bee.title: Introduction to Mechanical Bees
ponder.cbbees.portable_beehive.title: The Portable Beehive
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive.text_1: The Mechanical Beehive is the home of your bees. Each beehive can keep one type of bee
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive.text_2: Bees are inserted with funnels or hoppers
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive.text_3: Without rotation, no bee leaves the hive
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive.text_4: Jobs placed in the range of a Mechanical Beehive can be worked on by the bees inside it
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive.text_5: When the work is done, they return to the hive to rewind their springs
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive_speed.t: A hive only takes jobs within its range
This build is out of range, so no bee will come
Faster rotation increases its range, how many bees fly at once and how fast they fly
Now the build is in reach
Engineer's Goggles show its network, bees and spring efficiency
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_beehive_network: Each hive covers its own range
A build further away can't be reached
Hives placed in each other's range join one network. Together they reach every build in any of their ranges
Ports in range join the network too, so every bee in it can use them
Bees of every hive work together. The closest hive with free bees is asked first
cbbees.ponder.logistics_port.text_1: Bees need the materials for every block they place
cbbees.ponder.logistics_port.text_2: But they can't take anything out of an inventory on their own
cbbees.ponder.logistics_port.text_3: A Logistics Port lets bees take items from the inventory it sits on
cbbees.ponder.logistics_port.text_4: If several ports offer an item, the one with the highest priority is used first
cbbees.ponder.logistics_port.text_5: Now bees pick up the items they need and get to work
cbbees.ponder.logistics_port.text_6: Switched to INSERT with a wrench, a port stores what bees bring back, like blocks from a deconstruction
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_1: Farms and machines fill up their inventory far away from where the items are needed
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_2: Cargo Ports are Providers when placed
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_3: A wrench switches a port to Requester
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_4: Ports with the same frequency item belong together, shown by a line between them
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_5: Mechanical Bumble Bees pick up new items from the Provider and deliver them to the Requester
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_6: With several Requesters on a frequency, the one with the highest priority is served first, not the closest
cbbees.ponder.cargo_port.text_7: Bumble Bees deliver everything they carry. If the destination runs out of space, the leftover items are dropped next to it
cbbees.ponder.dock_port.text_1: Some builds need fluids, like the water in this fountain
cbbees.ponder.dock_port.text_2: Bees can't drain a tank on their own
cbbees.ponder.dock_port.text_3: A Dock Port lets bees take fluids from the tank it sits on
cbbees.ponder.dock_port.text_4: Bees carry the fluid over and place it
cbbees.ponder.dock_port.text_5: Switched to INSERT with a wrench, a Dock Port stores fluids bees bring back
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.header: Requesting materials with the Waggle Port
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_1: Bees build with what their network holds, while your Create logistics network may hold much more
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_2: When a job is missing materials, the bees can only wait
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_3: Tuned on a Stock Link before placing, the Waggle Port joins that logistics network
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_4: Placed in the bee network, it orders whatever a job is missing
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_5: Its orders are sent to the address set in the Waggle Port
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_6: A Packager with a matching address sign unpacks the deliveries next to a Logistics Port
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_7: The bees pick the delivery up and finish the job
cbbees.ponder.waggle_port.text_8: Items your Factory Gauges keep in stock are crafted automatically and requested again until the job is done
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_bee.text_1: The Mechanical Bee builds and takes down blocks, and places fluids
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_bee.text_2: The Mechanical Bumble Bee carries items between Cargo Ports, up to three stacks per trip
cbbees.ponder.mechanical_bee.text_3: Each hive keeps one type of bee
cbbees.ponder.bee_spring.text_1: Every bee runs on a clockwork spring
cbbees.ponder.bee_spring.text_2: Each block it places or breaks winds the spring down a little
cbbees.ponder.bee_spring.text_3: When the spring runs out, the bee flies home to rewind it
cbbees.ponder.bee_spring.text_4: Then it gets back to work where it stopped
cbbees.ponder.bee_spring.text_5: Faster rotation rewinds springs quicker and makes them last longer
cbbees.ponder.bee_spring.text_6: Bees from a Portable Beehive pay for every rewind with honey

gui.cbbees.tool.program.desc: Right-click to program schematic into a reusable item
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer.text_1: A Programmed Schematic stores a construction or deconstruction job made with a Planner
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer.text_2: On its own, the stored job never starts
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer.text_3: The Schematic Deployer holds a Programmed Schematic and starts its job
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer.text_4: A redstone pulse deploys the job
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer.text_5: A comparator reads its state: empty (0), loaded (1), working (8) or just deployed (15)
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer.text_6: Hoppers and pipes can insert and take out Programmed Schematics
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer_automat: In Absolute mode, the job is built at the coordinates it was programmed with
Moving the Deployer doesn't move the build
In Relative mode, the build is placed relative to the Deployer instead
Wherever the Deployer is placed, the build follows
Relative mode can also rotate and mirror the build without reprogramming
cbbees.ponder.schematic_deployer_self_re: A schematic can contain a Schematic Deployer itself, like this bridge segment
A freshly built Deployer would be empty
Instead, it receives the program and settings of the Deployer that built it
In Relative mode, each Deployer builds the next segment, carrying the program forward
